notes: GPUI WIDGETS for the browser chrome. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React, and you have no training knowledge of its exact API. Before writing, read: rever/src/main.rs as it is in git HEAD (`git show HEAD:rever/src/main.rs`; the file on disk is being rewritten by someone else right now, do not edit anything under rever/) for the current simple tab strip, the finished crates as worked examples (rever-ui-menus for popups, rever-ui-traffic, rever-ui-history: their src and examples/preview.rs), every file in rever-ui-kit/src, and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs plus vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs (drag_drop.rs for dragging) for exact method names. Build: (1) the tab bar from TabBar.tsx as a view implementing gpui::Render: tabs with title, profile label and the dot for isolated tabs, the active tab styling, close buttons, middle-click close, the new-tab button, and the Chrome-style overflow where tabs that do not fit move into a '⋯ N' menu while the active tab always stays visible; the tab data comes from rever-ui-state's tabs store types, and select/close/new-tab are emitted as GPUI events; keep the fit computation a plain function with unit tests. (2) use-resizable.ts as a reusable resizable splitter: a drag handle element plus the size state with min, max, initial value and persistence key (rever-ui-state Storage), for both axes. (3) use-find-in-page.ts as the find bar view (query field, match count, next, previous, close, Escape) with the actual searching behind a trait the host implements. (4) MarkupEditor.tsx as its view with the same tools and behaviors. Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css (tokens in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; define a missing one locally and list it). User-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the keys the TSX uses. Keep logic in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; a file gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-chrome --example preview_chrome` shows a tab bar narrow enough to overflow, a splitter between two panes, the find bar and the markup editor; capture with `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_chrome /tmp/preview_chrome.png`, read the PNG, compare with the TSX, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, do not run the `rever` app, and never run cargo without `-p` (other crates in the workspace are mid-edit).
